request.prompt: How many commercial humanoid robots exist?

result.text:
While traditional industrial robots have surpassed an operational global stock of 5 million units, commercial humanoid robots (bipedal or full-size humanoids over 140 cm designed for professional work rather than R&D or entertainment) represent a much smaller, emerging market.

According to data released by the

International Federation of Robotics (IFR)

in their

World Robotics report

, roughly 7,000 full-size commercial humanoid units were sold globally in a single recent annual tracking period.

Key Market Breakdown

Annual Sales & Deployment: While media hype surrounds humanoids, they still constitute a tiny fraction of the broader robotics sector. Total global sales for full-size commercial humanoids sit around 7,000 units annually, with early deployments heavily concentrated in pilot programs, logistics handling, and controlled manufacturing environments.

Growth Trajectory: According to market tracking by

IDC on Humanoid Robotics Commercialization Trends

, global shipments are accelerating rapidly with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) near 95%, expecting cumulative shipments to eclipse 510,000 units by 2030.

Adoption Hurdles: Widespread scaling is still constrained by high maintenance/training costs, evolving safety standards, and the fact that many deployments still rely partially on human teleoperation rather than full autonomy.

If you're looking into specific aspects of the market, I can provide details on:

Top manufacturers leading commercial humanoid production
Primary industries adopting humanoids (e.g., automotive logistics, warehousing)
Cost vs. ROI models for deploying humanoids right now
